title: Open finite-presentation charts of an fpqc form spread along affine limits
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $p:A\to S$ be a flat surjective quasi-compact morphism with $A$ affine [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and let $F$ be a contravariant set-valued functor on $S$-schemes satisfying the fpqc covering equalizer condition. Suppose $F_A$ is represented by an $A$-scheme $P$ quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-representable-functor, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(T_i)$ an inverse system of affine $S$-schemes with limit $T$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with its specified projections [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $F_T$ is represented by a scheme $Y$. Let $V\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] of finite presentation over $T$, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. There are $i\in I$, a $T_i$-scheme $V_i$ of finite presentation, and a map of fpqc sheaves $h_{V_i}\to F_{T_i}$ which is a representable open immersion: its pullback along every map $h_H\to F_{T_i}$ from a scheme is represented by an open subscheme of $H$. Its base change to $T$ is the specified inclusion $h_V\subseteq F_T$, through an isomorphism $V_i\times_{T_i}T\simeq V$. If $V$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, $V_i$ may also be chosen quasi-affine. No representability of $F_{T_i}$ is assumed.

source.place: Raynaud, Un critere d effectivite de descente, Theorem 4.1 proof, reductions 3 and 4, printed pp.5-19--5-20. Primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](1) to $V\to T$. The affine stages are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and their transition maps, being maps of affine schemes, are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Obtain $i_0$, a finitely presented $T_{i_0}$-scheme $V_{i_0}$, and a specified isomorphism $V_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T\simeq V$. For $j\ge i_0$ put $V_j=V_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_j$. These schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; their transition maps are affine and their limit is $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products].

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), Tag 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), Tag 01Z5 (lemma-limit-quasi-affine); Raynaud Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, after the separatedness reduction 2.

proof.text: Under the functor-of-points interpretation, the given inclusion $h_V\to F_T$ gives a section $v\in F(V)$: evaluate on $1_V$. Conversely a section gives a natural transformation by restriction along each map to $V$. Apply [lem-sfb-fpqc-form-qcqs-limit-continuity] to the system $V_j$. After enlarging $i_0$ obtain $v_i\in F(V_i)$ restricting to $v$, hence a map $h_{V_i}\to F_{T_i}$, where the prescribed $T_i$-coordinate is retained. Base change identifies this map with the specified inclusion, not merely an abstract isomorphic chart.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), Tag 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), Tag 01Z5 (lemma-limit-quasi-affine); Raynaud Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, after the separatedness reduction 2.

proof.text: Put $B_j=A\times_ST_j$, $B=A\times_ST$ and $W_j=A\times_SV_j$. The $B_j$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and $W_j$ is finitely presented over $B_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; these are affine-transition systems with the displayed limits by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products]. The section $v_i$ gives a scheme map $a_i:W_i\to P\times_AB_i$. Its limit is the base change of $V\hookrightarrow Y$, hence an open immersion. The source $W_i$ is quasi-compact. Cover its image in $P$ by finitely many affine opens and let $P_0$ be their union. Then $a_i$ factors through $P_0\times_AB_i$. Since $P/A$ is quasi-separated and $A$ affine, $P$ is quasi-separated; the open $P_0$ is qcqs. Local finite presentation restricts to this open, so $P_0/A$ is finitely presented. Thus both $W_i$ and $P_0\times_AB_i$ are qcqs.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), Tag 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), Tag 01Z5 (lemma-limit-quasi-affine); Raynaud Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, after the separatedness reduction 2.

proof.text: The map $W_i\to P_0\times_AB_i$ is locally of finite presentation. Here is the elementary affine verification from [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]: for affine charts over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B_i$, their rings $C,D$ are finitely presented over $R$. Write $C=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$, $D=R[u_1,\ldots,u_e]/(s_1,\ldots,s_f)$, and choose polynomials $q_l(t)$ for the images of $u_l$ in $C$. The given $D$-algebra $C$ has finite presentation $D[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m,u_1-q_1,\ldots,u_e-q_e)$. Its identification with $C$ follows by eliminating the $u_l$; each $s_b(q)$ vanishes modulo the $r_a$. These charts establish the assertion.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), Tag 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), Tag 01Z5 (lemma-limit-quasi-affine); Raynaud Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, after the separatedness reduction 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-open-immersion-qcqs] over the affine system $B_j$, on the tail starting at $i$. Step 3 supplies qcqs sources and targets, step 4 local finite presentation, and the limiting map is an open immersion by step 3. For some $j\ge i$ the map $W_j\to P_0\times_AB_j$ is an open immersion. Its composite into $P\times_AB_j$ is therefore an open immersion too. Replace $i,V_i,v_i$ by this $j,V_j,v_j$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), Tag 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), Tag 01Z5 (lemma-limit-quasi-affine); Raynaud Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, after the separatedness reduction 2.

proof.text: For any $T_i$-scheme $H$ and section $h\in F(H)$, put $H_A=H\times_SA$. The pullback of $h_{V_i}\to F_{T_i}$ on $H_A$ is represented by an open $E'\subset H_A$, since its further description is the scheme pullback of the open immersion $W_i\to P\times_AB_i$ along the section $H_A\to P\times_AB_i$. On $H_A\times_HH_A$ the two opens agree: on every test they both express the equality between the prescribed $F$-section and the section from $V_i$, with its $T_i$-coordinate. The cover $H_A\to H$ is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] gives an open $E\subset H$. It represents the original pullback: for every $K\to H$, a lift $K\to V_i$ implies $K_A\to H_A$ lands in $E'$. Conversely, if $K\to H$ lands in $E$, the unique local lift $K_A\to V_i$ has equal restrictions to the double overlap, because $W_i\to P\times_AB_i$ is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] it descends uniquely to $K\to V_i$ over $T_i$. The equality of its section with $h|_K$ holds after the fpqc cover and therefore on $K$, by the equalizer condition on $F$. These inverse constructions are natural. Thus $h_{V_i}\to F_{T_i}$ is a representable open immersion.

source.place: Tag 03N0 (lemma-open-fpqc-covering), Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); applied to the explicit pullback subfunctor.

proof.text: If $V$ is quasi-affine, apply [lem-sfb-limit-quasi-affine-eventual] to the qcqs affine-transition system $V_j$ on the present tail. Its limit is the specified $V$, so a later $V_j$ is quasi-affine. Replace the chart by that base change. Its finite presentation persists by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its representable open-immersion property persists directly: a scheme test at $T_j$ is also one at $T_i$, and its pullback is the same open with the fixed $T_j$-coordinate. The specified isomorphism and inclusion at $T$ persist as well.
